newsitem.title: USA: Houston Industries nears closing on merger.
newsitem.headline: Houston Industries nears closing on merger.

text.p: Houston Industries Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Don Jordan said Wednesday he expects the company's merger with NorAm Energy Corp to close in mid-February.
Jordan said he sees no hurdles in obtaining remaining federal and state approvals for the deal, which would form a $14.3 billion combined electric and natural gas company.

The $3.9 billion merger, which will form the nation's third-largest combined electric and gas company serving 3.6 million customers in six states, was subject to approval from the state and federal regulators.

"We now have approval in all of the states with the exception of Minnesota and with all the regulatory groups with the exception of the Securities and Exchange Commission," Jordan said. "There are no intervenors and no opposition before either one of those agencies."
The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission also must approve transfer of a power trading license.
Jordan, 64, on June 1, 1999 plans to step down as chairman and chief executive of the Houston-based company, which today named Steve Letbetter president and chief operating officer.
Letbetter said the company is studying options for competing in the domestic electric generation business as states open up to competition grids now under monopoly control of local utilities.

But he said states opening their grids to competition are seeking to reduce relatively high electric costs and the Houston company will urge Texas legislators convening this year to go slow in deregulating this state's electric system.
"We think it's prudent to stand back and observe rather than experimenting," he said.
The executives in an interview with reporters declined comment on potential international acquisitions, but said the company will budget $250 million a year on power projects overseas.
